display: If a human has to do it twice,
I want to know why software isn't.
prose: I trained as a mechanical engineer. What I actually did, most days, was watch competent people retype numbers between systems — and then write scripts so they wouldn't have to. That habit outgrew the discipline, and now it is the work: I design and ship production-grade agents, voice pipelines and internal tools that remove repetitive labour at scale.

The mechanical background left a bias I've kept. A workflow is a machine: it has tolerances, failure modes and a duty cycle. Most AI projects fail not on model quality but on the unglamorous parts — retries, idempotency, what happens when the third-party API returns HTML instead of JSON at 2am.
So I build for the boring case first. Then the demo takes care of itself.

contact.display: Have a process that eats your week?
contact.lede: Tell me the boring version of it — the spreadsheet, the inbox, the phone that keeps ringing. That's usually where the good automation is hiding.
